summary: Masaaki Hattori worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, holding posts at Kyoto University from 1955 and 1961 to 1988, and later at Osaka Gakuin University in 1989.

Masaaki Nitta studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1968). He held professorial posts at Fukui Prefectural College (~1975–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Masaaki Nohnin studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as associate professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
Working in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Masaaki Tsuchiya studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979–1988). He took up a post at Senshu University around 1997.

Masaharu Anesaki studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, working in religious and Buddhist studies. He became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 1904, serving as its library director from 1923 to 1934.

Masaharu Imai studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1970–1977), working in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He was an associate professor at Ibaraki University (1977) and later became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba (2006).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Masahide Mori studied at Nagoya University and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Nagoya University (~1996–2000) and Kanazawa University as associate professor and professor from ~2000.
Masahiro Asada studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1973) in the field of Buddhist studies. He later served as an associate professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Masahiro Inami specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing graduate studies at Hiroshima University (~1985–1990). He subsequently held academic posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (attested 1998, ~2006).

Masahiro Kusunoki worked in religious studies and philosophy after studying at Tohoku University (~1948–1953). He served as professor and chair of religious studies and history of religion at Tohoku University from ~1968 to 1985.

Masahiro Shimoda studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Delhi, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and joined Musashino University as professor in 2023.
Masahiro Takano studied in the doctoral program at Taisho University, specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a post as a librarian at Taisho University (attested 1995).

Masakazu Tanaka studied at Tohoku University and the London School of Economics, focusing on religious studies and Indology. He served as associate professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and became vice president and professor at Professional Institute of International Fashion in 2019.

Masako Keta studied philosophy and religious studies at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi and Shōtō Hase. She served as professor at Kanazawa University in 1998 and later as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1957 and held an academic post there from ~1971 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo studied at Otani University, Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao, and in the US, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctorate in philosophy from the University of Vienna, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Helmut Krasser in 2006.

Masanori Nakagawa worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty at Chikushi Jogakuen University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1991 and as an associate professor of literature in 2002.

Masanori Shono is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe studied at Kyoto, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary under Hajime Tanabe and Daisetsu Suzuki. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Kyoto, Hanazono, and Nara universities, and the University of Hawaiʻi.
